name: MonarchAiTonePicker
title: AiTonePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton rows with androidx.compose.foundation.selection.selectable in a selectableGroup (cards); androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox (compact); MonarchTextField for the custom tone
summary: Chooses the tone the assistant writes in: Professional, Technical, Casual and Executive by default, each with a one-line description, and an optional custom tone in the person's own words.
whenToUse: In assistant settings or next to a prompt, where the person picks how the reply should read.
whenNotToUse: For other single choices use MonarchRadioRow in a selectableGroup. For a length or format setting use a segmented button.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTonePicker(selection: String, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tones: List<MonarchAiTone> = MonarchAiTone.defaults(), variant: MonarchAiTonePickerVariant = MonarchAiTonePickerVariant.Cards, enabled: Boolean = true, customText: String = "", onCustomTextChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, label: String? = null, customLabel: String? = null, customDetail: String? = null, customFieldLabel: String? = null, customPrompt: String? = null)
data class MonarchAiTone(id: String, label: String, detail: String)
companion object MonarchAiTone.Companion { const val CUSTOM_ID: String = "custom"; @Composable fun defaults(): List<MonarchAiTone> }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected tone, or MonarchAiTone.CUSTOM_ID for the Custom option.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the id of the tone the user chose.

options.name: tones
options.description: The tones to offer, each with an id, a label and a one-line detail.

options.name: variant
options.description: Cards: one row per tone with its description. Compact: a field that opens a menu.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the tone.

options.name: customText
options.description: The person's own description of the tone.

options.name: onCustomTextChange
options.description: Called as the custom description changes. Passing it adds the Custom option and, while it is selected, a text field.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the name of the choice, "Tone".

options.name: customLabel
options.description: Replaces the name of the Custom option.

options.name: customDetail
options.description: Replaces the description of the Custom option.

options.name: customFieldLabel
options.description: Replaces the label of the custom text field.

options.name: customPrompt
options.description: Replaces the placeholder of the custom text field.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row has the subtle assistant fill, a 2dp assistant border and a filled radio mark in the solid assistant color.

states.name: not selected
states.description: A surface row with a 1dp default border and an empty radio mark.

states.name: custom selected
states.description: A MonarchTextField for the custom tone appears under the options.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Rows use the disabled text color and do not respond; the selected row keeps its thicker border and filled mark.

states.name: compact
states.description: A read-only outlined field labelled with the name of the choice; activating it opens a menu of the tone names.

appearance: Rows use the medium radius, the surface fill and the default border; the selected row uses the subtle assistant fill and the assistant border. Labels use the body type and descriptions the caption type in the muted text color, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web lays the cards in a grid of columns at least 176px wide; Android shows one column, as iOS does, which holds at every font size. The web's compact variant is a native select; Android uses the Material 3 exposed dropdown menu, whose arrow icon comes from Material 3. The web's uncontrolled custom text (defaultCustomText) is not offered: pass customText and onCustomTextChange. MonarchAiTone.defaults() is a composable function because the built-in names and descriptions are string resources.
accessibility: In cards each tone is one row with the radio button role, read as its label and description, and the rows are a selectableGroup, so TalkBack reads the position in the list and the selected state.
The selected row is also marked by a filled radio mark and a thicker border, not by color alone.
The name of the choice is a visible text above the rows.
Every row is at least 48dp high and its text wraps at large font sizes.
The compact variant is the Material 3 exposed dropdown menu, labelled with the name of the choice.
The custom field is a MonarchTextField with its own label.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no tone shows no row as selected.
A tone whose id is "custom" is dropped while the Custom option is shown, so ids stay unique.
A tone with an empty detail shows only its label.
The custom text is kept when another tone is selected; the app decides whether to use it.

examples.title: Cards with a custom tone
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchAiTonePicker(
        selection = tone,
        onSelectionChange = { tone = it },
        tones = listOf(
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.0.id}}, {{tones.0.label}}, {{tones.0.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.1.id}}, {{tones.1.label}}, {{tones.1.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.2.id}}, {{tones.2.label}}, {{tones.2.description}}),
            MonarchAiTone({{tones.3.id}}, {{tones.3.label}}, {{tones.3.description}}),
        ),
        customText = customText,
        onCustomTextChange = { customText = it },
        label = {{messages.label}},
        customLabel = {{messages.custom}},
        customDetail = {{messages.customDescription}},
    )
    MonarchText(text = "Selected: " + tone)
}
examples.setupTemplate:
var tone by remember { mutableStateOf({{value}}) }
var customText by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
examples.setup:
var tone by remember { mutableStateOf("professional") }
var customText by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
examples.code:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2)) {
    MonarchAiTonePicker(
        selection = tone,
        onSelectionChange = { tone = it },
        tones = listOf(
            MonarchAiTone("professional", "Professional", "Clear, polite and to the point."),
            MonarchAiTone("technical", "Technical", "Precise terms, detail and structure."),
            MonarchAiTone("casual", "Casual", "Friendly and conversational."),
            MonarchAiTone("executive", "Executive", "Short, decision-first, no detail."),
        ),
        customText = customText,
        onCustomTextChange = { customText = it },
        label = "Tone",
        customLabel = "Custom",
        customDetail = "Describe the tone in your own words.",
    )
    MonarchText(text = "Selected: " + tone)
}

examples.title: Compact, with a custom tone
examples.setup:
var tone by remember { mutableStateOf(MonarchAiTone.CUSTOM_ID) }
var custom by remember { mutableStateOf("Warm but brief") }
examples.code:
MonarchAiTonePicker(
    selection = tone,
    onSelectionChange = { tone = it },
    variant = MonarchAiTonePickerVariant.Compact,
    customText = custom,
    onCustomTextChange = { custom = it },
)
